note: Eleventh round: added case 9 (case9-multi-fault-traced), the corpus's first OpenTelemetry-instrumented case and its first multi-fault one, to exercise R-VER-17 (attribute a multi-fault finding from real ingested spans). Whole corpus re-run 2026-08-09T00:16Z through the real binary. Case 9 reports confidence `caused`, cause dep_a_slow, with a two-hop chain read off real spans; no other case changed. Two real defects were found building it and fixed: trace ingestion could not reach a Jaeger inside the DC-2-isolated stack (no published host port) and now uses the same in-stack transport as the Prometheus client; and the degradation gate's bare 2x ratio was cleared by sub-millisecond jitter on an UNDISTURBED dependency (587us -> 1.3ms), which made one real cause and one noisy neighbour read as two candidates -- the gate now also requires a 10ms absolute step. Also corrected a factual error carried in the previous summary and in BENCHMARKS.md: cases 3, 6 and 7 are ambiguous because they declare NO faults, not because several were active.

case4_nonidempotent_consumer.defect: Non-idempotent consumer: applies its side effect (an in-memory counter increment) for every message it reads off a Redpanda topic, with no per-message dedup check at all.
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.fault: duplicate: 1.0 on target 'orders' (a topic name, not a host:port), at: peak for: 5s -- internal/queuefault's BrokerApplier, driving Redpanda's Pandaproxy (Kafka REST Proxy v2-compatible) over plain HTTP, exactly as internal/applier/broker_applier.go documents.
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.assert_form_used: promql: 'orders_processed_total <= orders_received_total' -- the ONLY assert form that could express this defect. k6 thresholds cannot see it at all: every POST /order still returns 202 whether or not the message is later processed twice, so no duration/failure-rate threshold would ever break. sql: reads as permanently unevaluated (no SQL execution path exists in v0, confirmed by reading internal/run/findings.go's evaluateSQLAsserts). promql: is fully evaluable given a live Prometheus and -prom-url -- confirmed by reading internal/run/findings.go's evaluatePromqlAsserts, which only reports 'not evaluated' when the querier is nil.
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.candidates_reason: Same structural gap as poison_pill/duplicate always hits: buildCandidates(fault, deps, lang) looks up depForTarget(deps, f.Target) by exact Dep.Address match, which is always host:port-shaped for every other fault verb -- but queuefault.Translate uses f.Target as a bare topic name (Topic: f.Target), which can never match a Dep.Address. This means D-9 candidates are structurally impossible for poison_pill/duplicate findings specifically, regardless of whether the underlying broker (Redpanda here, a recognized image type) is itself detected -- a narrower, more specific version of the case 1/2/5 gap. Reported, not patched (out of scope).
case4_nonidempotent_consumer.repeat_runs: 3/3 clean detections across repeat runs, confirming this isn't a fluke.

reachability_finding.title: CLOSED: internal/run can now reach a broker and Prometheus dual-homed inside the DC-2-isolated stack, with no workaround
reachability_finding.history: Round 8: BrokerApplier/HTTPPromQuerier had no join-the-namespace mechanism at all (plain connection-refused/EOF). Fixed in 562ffd2 with fallbackTransport (direct call, then a Docker network-namespace tunnel on failure). Round 9: the tunnel itself hardcoded 'localhost' as its dial target inside the joined netns, which BusyBox nc resolves to ::1 first with no IPv4 fallback -- broken against any IPv4-only listener (confirmed: Redpanda's Pandaproxy binds 0.0.0.0 only). Round 10 (this round): fixed in e39fe6e -- the tunnel now probes 127.0.0.1 then ::1 and uses whichever answers, instead of guessing.
reachability_finding.verification: Deleted evals/corpus/case4-nonidempotent-consumer/run.sh (the standalone dual-homed Redpanda/Prometheus workaround) entirely. Restored docker-compose.yml to plain compose-managed Redpanda + topic-init + Prometheus (no host-published ports needed on either). Ran `tortureu run -broker-url http://redpanda:8082 -prom-url http://prometheus:9090` directly -- the exact invocation a real user would write against their own docker-compose.yml, with no hand-built dual-homing of any kind. Case 4 detects: status:fail, correctly attributed to order_duplicate. The reachability finding is closed.
reachability_finding.secondary_observation_not_a_correctness_: The tunnel mechanism (one `docker run --rm` container per dialed HTTP request, since fallbackTransport builds a fresh http.Transport per RoundTrip) is expensive under repeated polling: BrokerApplier's redeliverOnce ticks every 500ms for the fault's whole duration, and each tick's GET/POST calls each open their own tunnel container. This round's case 4 run took 270s wall-clock and briefly held ~400 short-lived (self-removing, --rm) containers at once, versus roughly 30-90s and a handful of containers for every other corpus case. Nothing leaked (docker ps -a / docker network ls confirmed clean after the run finished) and the result was correct -- this is a cost observation, not a detection or correctness problem, and is not counted as a finding against the reachability fix.

secondary_findings_from_building_this_fi: Pandaproxy's own auto-create-topic-on-first-produce path hung for 5+ seconds per attempt rather than failing fast or succeeding quickly, in this Redpanda version/config -- pre-creating the topic explicitly (via rpk) sidesteps it entirely. Not a TortureU defect (Redpanda's own behavior), but worth recording since it shaped the fixture.

config.Parse's fault-target validation (`knownTargets`) is purely syntactic -- built only from the SUT's own service name and torture.yaml's own declared egress.hosts keys, with no access to detect.System -- so a queue-fault's topic-shaped target has to be declared in egress.hosts even though internal/run's own queuefault routing never actually consults that classification for poison_pill/duplicate (unlike error_rate, which IS checked against class: mock). The declaration is required to pass the parser and then entirely inert. Not a bug -- config.Parse cannot see detect.System's output by design -- but a real rough edge for anyone writing a queue-fault torture.yaml.

metrics.detection: 8/8 planted defects detected (cases 1-7 and 9). Case 8 (control) correctly found nothing.
metrics.attribution: 5/8 findings-bearing cases named a causing fault (1, 2, 4, 5, 9) = 62.5%, which is BELOW this project's 70% bar and is reported as such. Cases 3, 6 and 7 declare no faults at all, so there is no candidate cause for any mechanism to name -- they are a permanent floor on this denominator, not a fixable miss. On the denominator attribution can affect (findings from runs that had faults) it is 5/5, including the one multi-fault case, which is 1/1.
metrics.candidates: 2/7 findings-bearing cases carry a candidate list: case 3 (pgx -- MaxConns, the exactly-right knob) and case 7 (go-redis, present and honestly caveated). Cases 1, 2, 4, 5 carry none -- three distinct, precisely diagnosed structural reasons, all reported rather than routed around: (a) a custom application image outside detect's closed vocabulary never becomes a detect.Dep (cases 1, 2, 5); (b) net/http can never be discovered as a client via manifest scanning regardless of vocabulary, since it's stdlib and never appears in a go.mod require line, and internal/detect's own recognition table has no net/http entry either (cases 1, 2, 5); (c) a queue-fault's topic-shaped target can never match a Dep.Address, which is always host:port-shaped (case 4). Case 6 correctly carries none (in-process queue, no client library exists to find).
metrics.false_positive_on_control: 0, across 21+ consecutive case-8 runs spanning seven different code-path states. Never non-zero once actually measured.
metrics.confidence: 1/1: the only OTel-instrumented case (9) reaches `caused` with a real chain; the seven cases with no tracing top out at `correlated`. That is D-4's claim, now measured on both sides.

make_eval.status: wired, complete, and re-verified end to end this round with all 7 built cases plus the control -- no case-specific workaround remains anywhere in the corpus
make_eval.what_it_does: evals/run_case.sh: builds the real tortureu binary, builds each case's pre-built dependency image, runs every evals/corpus/case*/torture.yaml through the real binary (case 4 now gets its -broker-url/-prom-url flags from a plain per-case EXTRA_ARGS table, no special runner script), tears down every case's compose stack unconditionally, and exits non-zero if case 8 produced any findings.
make_eval.verified: Full `make eval` run this round (case 4 using plain compose-managed Redpanda/Prometheus, no workaround): all 7 built cases ran and detected their planted defect, case 8 passed with 0 findings, exit 0, and docker ps -a / docker network ls showed nothing left over afterward.

case9_multi_fault_traced.defect: Two faults active at once (dep-a slowed 3s via Toxiproxy, dep-b taken down), with the SUT calling dep-a with no timeout and dep-b with a 200ms timeout it tolerates. Only dep-a is on the path that breaks the SLO.
case9_multi_fault_traced.instrumentation: Go SUT with the real OpenTelemetry SDK exporting OTLP/HTTP spans to a jaegertracing/jaeger:2.10.0 service in its own compose stack. Client spans carry server.address/server.port, which is what internal/trace matches a fault target against.
case9_multi_fault_traced.why_it_matters: R-VER-3's fault-count rule can only call this finding ambiguous. The attribution comes entirely from the spans: exactly one of the two fault targets showed measured degradation.
case9_multi_fault_traced.harness_note: run_case.sh gained a per-case EXTRA_ENV table so this case can set TORTUREU_TRACE_URL=http://jaeger:16686 -- the default probe (localhost:16686) cannot work, because DC-2 enforcement leaves the stack's Jaeger with no published host port.
